sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) Work centres should be arranged in a ________ order to assist in the smooth flow of work. (b) Storage bins should be ________ so that contents can be seen.
Fill in the blanks. (a) All work centres in the kitchen should have adequate ________. (b) To save floor space, cupboards should be replaced with ________ storage.
State True or False. (a) A bedroom can be used for studying during the day. (b) Electric points can be placed anywhere in the bathroom.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: they should be kept away from water.

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Functional storage (b) Dead storage. B: (i) Storing rarely used items in high places (ii) Storing things near where they are used (iii) Storing things in a refrigerator.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What two essential provisions each would you ensure in a kitchen and a bathroom?
questions.answer: Kitchen: a convenient height for storage and a source of water with a washing area. Bathroom: a non-slippery sloping floor with drainage, and electrical points away from water.

questions.q: Why is it important to arrange things in an orderly manner at home?
questions.answer: It saves time and energy in finding things and looks neat and attractive. It also gives a feeling of more space and makes cleaning easy.

questions.q: What is a work centre?
questions.answer: The area specified for an activity at home is a work centre. It need not be a separate room; similar activities can share one room.

questions.q: Differentiate between functional storage and dead storage.
questions.answer: Functional storage keeps the things for a task near the place of the task. Dead storage keeps rarely used things in less accessible high places.

questions.q: List any two ways of saving space in a bedroom.
questions.answer: Use pull-out or bunk beds and beds with drawers for storage. Fix a mirror on the wall instead of a dressing table and build the almirah into the wall.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain space organisation and its significance (three points).
questions.answer: (i) It is assigning space to an activity and arranging all the required materials systematically. (ii) It saves time and energy because everything is available on the spot. (iii) It makes effective use of limited space, such as the living room being used for sleeping at night.

questions.q: List the guidelines for making a work centre more effective.
questions.answer: (i) Arrange work centres in a sequential order and have transparent or labelled containers. (ii) Provide adequate lighting and ventilation and keep centres easy to clean. (iii) Prefer built-in storage and use space under the staircase, window slabs and lofts.

questions.q: How can aesthetics be created in a work area? (three points)
questions.answer: (i) Furniture of suitable size and an organised look. (ii) Good lighting and light colours that make rooms look bright and spacious. (iii) Decorative items and indoor plants, without blocking movement.

questions.q: Suggest space-saving ideas for a one-room house (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Use a diwan, sofa-cum-bed and folding beds for sleeping. (ii) Use a folding dining or study table fixed on the wall and built-in storage. (iii) Mark and distinguish the cooking, sleeping and sitting areas by screens or furniture.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the space management of the kitchen and bathroom, including kitchen layouts.
questions.answer: (i) Things used often are stored at a convenient height, heavy containers at floor level and rare items in dead storage. (ii) A utensil washing area should be near the cooking area. (iii) Layouts are one-walled, two-walled, L-shaped and U-shaped, in sitting or standing kitchens. (iv) A folding wall table saves space for dining. (v) A bathroom needs storage for toiletries, water supply, sloping non-slippery floor, and electric points away from water. (vi) A clothesline near the washing area avoids unnecessary movement.
